newsitem.title: USA: U.S. court denies quick appeal over Conrail.
newsitem.headline: U.S. court denies quick appeal over Conrail.

text.p: A federal appeals court denied a request by a group of Conrail Inc shareholders seeking to block a planned merger with CSX Corp, for an expedited appeal of a lower court ruling against the group.
In an order by a three-judge panel of the Third U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, Circuit Judge Walter Stapleton gave parties in the case until the week of February 3 to file briefs on the appeal.
The action appears to remove the last legal cloud over a December 23 Conrail shareholders meeting at which a key vote regarding the merger will be held.
The appeals court also accepted a request by Norfolk Southern Corp to withdraw its motion for expedited appeal in a similar suit.
Norfolk Southern asked for the withdrawal on November 21, after completion of the first step in the CSX-Conrail merger, but said then it would continue to fight the appeal on a regular time schedule.
Both Norfolk Southern and the shareholders group sued to block Conrail from merging with CSX without considering a rival offer from Norfolk Southern.
Norfolk Southern has launched a $110 per share, all-cash bid, worth $10 billion, for Conrail, as opposed to an $8.6 billion cash and stock deal between Conrail and CSX.

A U.S. District Court judge on November 19 declined to block the first stage of the merger -- a $110 per share tender offer by CSX for 19.9 percent of Conrail shares. The tender was completed on November 21.
But the shareholders group, arguing for a speedy appeal, had said the court could still intervene by blocking CSX from voting its newly acquired stake at the December 23 Conrail meeting.

Shareholders at the meeting will be asked to waive a Pennsylvania law that would force CSX to pay cash for all of Conrail once it had acquired a 20 percent stake. Parties involved have said the vote will be close.

Under a merger agreement between the two, CSX is to pay $110 per share cash for 40 percent of Conrail, and exchange stock at a rate of about 1.86 shares for each Conrail share for the remaining 60 percent.
That "back end" share swap was worth $87.24 per Conrail share at Tuesday's closing prices.
Conrail has said it was seeking an improved bid from CSX.
